title: What is MBB, and how do McKinsey, BCG and Bain differ?
description: What MBB means, what the three firms have in common, and the differences candidates notice in their interviews and cultures.
hook: MBB stands for McKinsey, BCG and Bain. You will hear the term constantly in case prep. The three firms are more alike than different, but there are real differences in how they interview, and knowing them helps you prepare properly for each.
body:
What they have in common

  • Focus on senior-level strategy problems, alongside operations and implementation work.
  • Very selective hiring, with case interviews at the centre and a strong weight on fit or personal experience questions.
  • Similar career paths and an up-or-out promotion model.
  • Recruit from universities, business schools and experienced professionals.

How their interviews differ

  • McKinsey: cases are usually interviewer-led: the interviewer asks a series of questions and you answer each in turn. Every interview also includes a Personal Experience Interview, which gets as much weight as the case. Many candidates first take the online Solve assessment. Full McKinsey guide.
  • BCG: cases are usually candidate-led: you drive the case. BCG's own careers site describes a skill interview, a case interview and a team interview, and many offices use an online case with a chatbot called Casey. Full BCG guide.
  • Bain: cases are usually candidate-led, with a fit or experience interview alongside, and some offices use a written case in later rounds. Full Bain guide.

Culture

Each firm has a reputation (and plenty of stereotypes). The most reliable way to understand the differences is to talk to people who work there, ideally in the office you would join. Culture often varies more between offices and teams than between firms.

Should you apply to all three?

If you are aiming for strategy consulting, usually yes. The preparation overlaps by about 90%. Practise both interviewer-led and candidate-led cases, and prepare your stories for a deep personal experience interview.
